Sound Familiar?

Common Trauma Surgery Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Trauma activation fee not billed or not coordinated between physician and facility claims.

PMEX coordinates trauma activation billing with the facility team to confirm both physician and facility claims are consistent.

Open fracture billed as closed fracture, losing the higher open fracture treatment reimbursement.

PMEX reads the operative report to confirm fracture classification (open vs. closed) before selecting the treatment CPT code.

Critical care time not aggregated across multiple ICU documentation entries on the same day.

PMEX aggregates all critical care documentation entries per calendar day and bills 99291 and 99292 per the total time.

MVA injury filed to health insurance instead of the auto insurance carrier.

PMEX identifies MVA injuries at registration and routes claims to the correct auto insurance carrier before health insurance.

ORIF coded at a lower complexity level than the operative report supports.

PMEX reads every ORIF operative report and codes the fixation type and bone at the correct procedure level.

Workers comp injury filed to group health instead of the employer WC carrier.

PMEX implements WC identification at registration and routes all work-related injuries to the correct WC carrier.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Trauma Surgery Billing

Trauma practices lose 16 to 28 percent of revenue to activation billing gaps, fracture miscoding, and workers comp routing errors.

PATTERN 01

Open Fracture Treatment Billed as Closed

Gustilo Type II open tibia fracture treated with irrigation, debridement, and external fixation. Closed fracture treatment code submitted. Open fracture treatment codes reimburse at a significantly higher rate and reflect the complexity of the procedure performed.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reads the operative report to confirm Gustilo classification and operative technique for every fracture case. Open fracture treatment codes are applied when the report documents the wound, debridement, and open fracture management.

PATTERN 02

Trauma Critical Care Time Not Aggregated

Trauma surgeon documents 30 minutes of critical care at 6 AM during rounds and 35 minutes at 2 PM after a deterioration event. Total: 65 minutes. 99291 billed. 99292 not billed. A third 20-minute entry at 8 PM brings the total to 85 minutes. The third entry is not reviewed before billing. $120 in add-on revenue missed.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews all critical care documentation entries across the calendar day before coding trauma critical care, aggregating time to confirm whether 99292 add-on units are billable.

PATTERN 03

MVA Injury Billed to Health Insurance First

Patient presents after motor vehicle accident. Front desk registers to the health insurance card on file. Medical insurance processes and pays the claim. Six months later, auto insurance is identified as the primary payer. Health insurer demands recovery of payment already made.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX implements MVA identification at registration, confirming auto insurance carrier and policy before any claim is submitted. Auto insurance is billed as primary with health insurance as secondary only when the auto policy limits are exhausted.

Questions

Traumatology Billing Questions Answered

Trauma activation fees are typically billed by the facility. The physician trauma activation component is coordinated separately. We confirm both the facility and physician activation billing are consistent and do not create duplicate service flags.

Open fractures involve a break in the skin over the fracture site. Closed fractures do not. CPT codes are distinct for open and closed fracture treatment. We read the operative report to confirm fracture classification before selecting the treatment code.

Critical care time is cumulative for the calendar day. We aggregate all documented critical care time across chart entries and bill 99291 (first 30 to 74 minutes) and 99292 (each additional 30 minutes) per the total documented time.

We identify work-related injuries at registration and route claims to the correct WC carrier with WC-specific claim forms and first report of injury documentation. WC billing is managed as a separate workflow from health insurance billing.

Yes. We coordinate with the facility billing team to confirm consistency between the facility and physician trauma activation claims.

Within 30 days, with trauma activation coordination and workers comp routing workflows active from day one.
